summary: OpenAI is launching ChatGPT for Academic Researchers, a program giving up to 100,000 academic researchers free access to its frontier ChatGPT and Codex models, expanding from an initial 10,000 this summer through 2027, as part of a $250M+ commitment to external scientific research.

mechanisms.reason: A free-access program extending frontier model use to up to 100,000 researchers, alongside stated existing weekly usage of 1.3 million people generating 8.4 million science-related messages, raises aggregate inference volume.
mechanisms.quote: We’re introducing ChatGPT for Academic Researchers, a program that will give 100,000 researchers at selected academic institutions free access to our frontier models.

mechanisms.reason: The program grants expanded deep research capacity and larger context windows to participants, increasing per-request memory footprint.
mechanisms.quote: They will also have expanded deep research, higher usage limits, and larger context windows.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6 Sol's stated jump on FrontierMath Tier 4 (83% vs 72.5% for GPT-5.5) signals a meaningful reasoning gain worth evaluating for research-heavy workloads, though the benchmark is the lab's own citation.
practices.quote: On FrontierMath Tier 4, which measures research-level mathematical reasoning, GPT‑5.6 Sol scores 83%, compared with 72.5% for GPT‑5.5.

practices.reason: The document cites specific benchmark instruments (FrontierMath Tier 4, GeneBench Pro) that a team could look to for measuring research-grade reasoning and biological-analysis performance, though results are the lab's own and not independently replicated.
practices.quote: On GeneBench Pro, which evaluates complex biological data analysis and scientific reasoning, GPT‑5.6 Sol Pro solves 31.5% of tasks.
